I've used Windows all my life. As a young teen I experimented with Linux and even used Ubuntu 10.04 as my primary OS for a while. I then moved to Mint as my primary OS. Opensuse is known for their support and polished kde desktop, but I believe you can use any DE you prefer. You can also use it as a rolling release os with tumbleweed. Make sure to check out their forums, I am pretty sure they can help you should you run into any problems.

You'll need to familiarize yourself with both the software/repositories/package manager environments and you'll need to look into the KDE Desktop environment(if you choose default) and it would differ from other Desktop enviroments as far as file managers and layout goes. Most other things should be a similar experience in that you'll have a terminal you can input commands to and a graphical interface you can also use to navigate.
OpenSuse has always been really stable and polished for me. Good choice.
